clue.text: Fix house taken by patient type

parts.note: to house someone is to put them up for the night
Job, the biblical sufferer, is the proverbial patient man

explanation.surface: A patient sort of person moves in to repair a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like a verb about repairs, but it is the noun: a rigged outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A fix is a rigged arrangement, the same as a fraud set up in advance.

clue.text: Evening dress?

parts.note: read not as formal wear for the night but as clothing that makes everyone level and alike in appearance

explanation.walkthrough: Formal evening wear is the obvious reading; the question mark invites 'evening' as 'making even', and the outfit worn identically by a group does just that.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching clothes worn by a whole group make them all look alike, levelling appearance like something that evens.

clue.text: Deceitful junior employee

definitions.meaning: dishonest, done in a sly secret way
a hand (worker) who is under another

explanation.definitionFit: Sly and secretive means deceitful; split, the word is a subordinate worker, a lower 'hand'.

clue.text: No way to get into A Month in the Country

indicators.note: the letters for 'No way' are said to enter the month, so they sit inside it

parts.note: Jan is the short form of January
no, as nothing, is O (nought)
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A reference to Turgenev's play A Month in the Country, with no way in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Month in the Country' reads as the play's title; split it, 'Country' is the definition and 'Month' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern kingdom with Amman as its capital is a nation, a country.

clue.text: Sapper officer, a titled man

definitions.meaning: Sapper was the pen name of H. C. McNeile, whose hero is an ex-army captain
a man who gives his name to a book's title: the 1920 novel is named after this hero

explanation.walkthrough: A sapper is also an army engineer, so 'Sapper officer' looks like a military rank; here it is the author Sapper's hero. 'Titled' suggests a peer, but means named in a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Hugh Drummond, nicknamed after a tenacious dog breed, is the gentleman adventurer of Sapper's thrillers and the title of the first.

clue.text: Turn to largely solid style of architecture

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

indicators.note: most of the word, so the synonym for solid loses its last letter

parts.note: thick means dense or solid

explanation.surface: A suggestion to switch to a mostly solid building style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts the K from THICK to leave THIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed-arch medieval manner of building cathedrals is a named architectural style.

clue.text: Good bowling no runs for captain

parts.note: in cricket, an over is a spell of six balls bowled
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A captain is praised for a fine bowling spell that gave away no runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is a set of six deliveries; the surface reads like a scorecard, but each word is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal terms for the boss: 'guv' and 'skipper' each name the person in charge.

clue.text: Emperor being hard on pope

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so the letter for hard comes first

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
Adrian is the name of several popes, Adrian IV being the only English one

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor is harsh towards the pope.
explanation.walkthrough: There was in fact a pope of the same name as this emperor, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman ruler who built a wall across northern Britain was an emperor.

clue.text: Gymnastic feat from one on the wagon

definitions.meaning: a sideways handspring with arms and legs spread like spokes
literally a wheel fitted to a cart

explanation.definitionFit: A sideways handspring is a gymnastic move; split, the word is a wheel of a cart, which runs on a wagon.

clue.text: First half of play-school is more pleasant

definitions.meaning: the first part of the German-derived name for a nursery school, garten being the second
comparative of a word for gentle and good-natured

explanation.walkthrough: 'First half of' looks like a selection indicator, but taken as a whole the phrase is a definition: the front half of the word for a nursery school.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer and gentler means more pleasant; it is also the front of the word for nursery school.

clue.text: Bank, say, filled with a very fragrant plant

indicators.note: the lender is stuffed with the next letters, which go inside it

parts.note: a bank is an example of a lender, hence 'say'

explanation.surface: A bank stuffed with a strongly scented plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The purple-flowered shrub prized for its scent is a fragrant plant.

clue.text: Tie up estate in which Baskerville Hall, for example, is found

definitions.text: in which Baskerville Hall, for example, is found

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up
an estate is landed property, land

explanation.surface: Securing an estate that contains the Baskervilles' house.
explanation.walkthrough: Baskerville Hall is the house in Conan Doyle's The Hound of the Baskervilles, set on Dartmoor; the definition is a long description of where it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle sets Baskerville Hall amid open heath on Dartmoor, the kind of wild upland terrain named.

clue.text: Clergyman getting one to join partners in study

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman
I is the Roman numeral one
in bridge East and West are partners

explanation.surface: A vicar joins two partners in his study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partners' is a bridge convention: E and W play together, as do N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To go over and examine something critically is to study it.

clue.text: Discredit material for examination that is on the slide

definitions.text: material for examination that is on the slide
definitions.meaning: a sample spread on a microscope slide for examination

explanation.definitionFit: To slander someone is to discredit them; a sample spread thinly on a microscope slide for testing is the second sense.

clue.text: Demonstrated inhaling pot prelude to early grave

indicators.note: the protesters take in the next piece, so it goes inside them

parts.note: protesters who sat in held a sit-in demonstration
an urn is a pot or vase

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word, its prelude

explanation.surface: A protest where marijuana was smoked leads to an untimely death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' and 'inhaling' suggest cannabis, but pot is URN; 'grave' looks like a burial place yet means solemn.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloomy, sombre temperament is serious and grave.

clue.text: Not knowing region, can go for a spin

indicators.note: the letters are sent whirling round and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Unfamiliar with the area, a can goes spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun for lack of knowledge is the state of not knowing.

clue.text: Volunteers to enter a wood likely to burn, which would be a criminal loss

indicators.note: the volunteers go into the following letters, sitting inside them

parts.note: tinder is dry kindling that catches fire easily
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteers move into a fire-prone wood, which would be a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's reserve force of volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a convicted felon or traitor forfeited land and civil rights by this legal process, a loss imposed for crime.

clue.text: Pompous and grand, went ahead and avoided duties

parts.note: smug means self-satisfied, pompous
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
led means went in front, went ahead

explanation.surface: A self-important man pushed on regardless and dodged his responsibilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duties' looks like obligations, but means customs duties, taxes on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying goods past customs without paying tax evades the excise duties owed.

clue.text: Exchange book, showing sign of concern

parts.note: to trade is to exchange
Mark is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Swapping a book, someone shows signs of worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concern' looks like worry, but means a business, a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A registered logo identifies a business, a concern in its commercial sense.

clue.text: Evergreen is a bit spectacular, but useless

indicators.note: only a small part of the following words is taken, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A remark that an evergreen plant is showy but of no use.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the end of 'spectacular' and ends inside 'useless'.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry tree is a shrub that keeps its leaves all year, an evergreen.

clue.text: Stop activity of one manufacturing spirits?

definitions.meaning: the apparatus used to distil alcohol

explanation.definitionFit: To quieten or halt movement is one sense; the distilling apparatus that makes whisky is the other.

clue.text: Gifted person encountering barrier, in general

indicators.note: the barrier is placed inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: A talented person meets an obstacle, generally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gifted' suggests talent, but means having received a gift in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left a bequest in a will is a person who has been given a gift.

clue.text: Shouts out, having succeeded in difficult moments

indicators.note: the letter for succeeded goes inside the word for shouts

parts.note: cries are shouts
s is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone cries out after winning through hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning points of danger or trouble are difficult moments.

clue.text: Hood last out of bag for dressing up

parts.note: Robin Hood, the outlaw of Sherwood Forest

indicators.note: the final letter is drawn from the following word

explanation.surface: Taking a hood out of the bag last of all for a fancy-dress outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' looks like a garment for dressing up; it is the outlaw's surname, giving his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on ceremonial garments is getting dressed up.

clue.text: Shortly encourage to publicise stuff about union

indicators.note: turned about, so the whole run of letters reads backwards
cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them
to air a view is to publicise it
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Briefly urging someone to announce material about a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' looks like a noun, but is the verb 'cram'. 'Shortly' drops a letter, and 'about' turns the whole string EGAIRRAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock is the union of two people.

clue.text: Painting backed by label on favoured artist's technique

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece on another follows it, so the label comes after the favoured piece
placed beside the label, so the reversed painting follows it

parts.note: to be in with someone, or in fashion, is to be favoured
a tag is a label

indicators.note: turned back, so the painting word reads in reverse

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: A painting with a label on the back describes a favourite artist's method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns OIL into LIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Engraving a design into a surface, as on gems or seals, is a craft method of artists.

clue.text: Teased about being boring

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked for being dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid and dull means unexciting, boring.

clue.text: Came after opponents and took action

parts.note: in bridge East and North sit next to each other on opposing sides
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: A litigant went after rivals in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opponents' is a bridge convention: E and N are on opposite sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Followed as a result, coming next in time, means came after.

clue.text: Rejected shortening of county symbol — I had complaint

indicators.note: thrown back, so the whole run of letters reads backwards
cut short, so the emblem loses its last letter

parts.note: the red rose is the emblem of Lancashire
contracted, I had is I'd

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a shortened county emblem was rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire, an English county, has the red rose as its emblem. 'shortening of' trims RED ROSE to REDROS; with ID added, 'Rejected' turns REDROSID round.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment or illness is a medical complaint.
